title: Cobalt Systems - Private VPC Discovery
summary: Intro/discovery focused on Private/VPC deployment for Redwood. Customer needs VPC peering, private endpoints, regional constraints (EU data residency), and KMS integration. Discussed networking options, latency considerations, and migration path from hosted to private. Agreed next steps: share security pack, network diagram template, and schedule a SE-led design workshop + pilot benchmark windows.
topics: Regional availability and EU data residency

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-31
Time: 16:00 PST / 19:00 EST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Erin Patel (Redwood AE), Jamal Ortiz (Redwood SE), Maya Lin (Cobalt CTO), Carlos Ruiz (Head of Infra), Priya Desai (Security)

---
00:00 Erin Patel: Hi everyone thanks for joining on the last day of the year, I appreciate you carving out time. quick round of intros?
00:08 Maya Lin: hi, Maya Lin, CTO at Cobalt, we own platform and infra, happy to dig in.
00:12 Carlos Ruiz: Carlos here, infra lead, networking and cloud stuff.
00:15 Priya Desai: Priya, security and compliance.
00:18 Erin Patel: Awesome. Jamal, you want to do a quick intro?
00:21 Jamal Ortiz: yeah hi all, Jamal Ortiz, SE on the Redwood infra team, I focus on private deployments and network designs, happy to go into nitty gritty.
00:30 Erin Patel: Goal for today is to understand your networking constraints and compliance needs so we can recommend hosted vs dedicated vs private — sounds like private VPC is where you're leaning?
00:39 Maya Lin: yes, for sure. we have data residency needs in EU and also internal policy that no model inference traffic leaves our VPC. so private endpoint or peering is required. also want KMS integration for keys.
00:55 Jamal Ortiz: totally, that makes sense. can you walk me through your existing infra? vpc layouts, regions, and whether you use transit gateway or direct connect?
01:03 Carlos Ruiz: we run primarily in eu-west-1 and us-east-1. production workloads and customer data must stay in eu-west-1. we use TGW for inter-region connectivity and have a managed VPN to on-prem. we prefer not to punch public endpoints through NAT for inference.
01:18 Jamal Ortiz: good to know. Redwood Private supports several network topologies — VPC peering, TGW attachments, and private endpoints (we call them PrivateLink-style endpoints). each has trade-offs around scale and cross-account routing.
01:30 Maya Lin: quick clarification, PrivateLink is the AWS term, do you require AWS-specific setup or is there an overlay option?
01:36 Jamal Ortiz: our private deployment uses cloud-native primitives. for AWS it's VPC endpoint services (NLB fronted) and optionally peering or TGW attachments. for other clouds it's similar but names differ. we also offer a hybrid option where the control plane is customer-managed in your VPC — some customers run the control plane in our managed account but use dedicated peering.
01:54 Priya Desai: KMS — we need CMKs in our account and no key material leaving our control. is there an HSM integration?
02:01 Jamal Ortiz: yes, we integrate with customer-managed KMS keys. for AWS that means you can provide a CMK in your account; Redwood's service account is granted Decrypt/Encrypt as needed with strict IAM. HSM-only keys are supported via external KMS in some setups, we can map the usage in the design workshop.
02:17 Carlos Ruiz: what about network egress? we want zero egress into the public internet for inference. how do we ensure that?
02:24 Jamal Ortiz: in Private you deploy the serving nodes into your VPC and attach an internal NLB. Traffic never goes through a public IP. we also support VPC peering to your application VPC or a cross-account TGW attach. there are firewall rules for outbound updates, but we can restrict those to specific IP ranges or use a bastion for patching.
02:41 Maya Lin: patch/update windows are a concern — we need maintenance windows and a rollback plan.
02:46 Erin Patel: SLA-wise we offer options via Dedicated/reserved capacity. for Private deployments there's an enterprise package with uptime targets and a runbook. Jamal will show typical maintenance cadence.
02:56 Jamal Ortiz: typically monthly non-critical updates, with emergency patches as needed. for zero-downtime we recommend multi-AZ placements and a canary rollout.
03:08 Carlos Ruiz: region constraint: inference must be in eu-west-1. can you pin model versions and serving to that region only?
03:15 Jamal Ortiz: yes, you can pin model versions and have serving pools restricted to a region. we also support routing policies so traffic from your EU app VPC goes to EU-serving pools only.
03:25 Priya Desai: audit logs — we need request logs and key rotation history for audits. how long do you retain logs? can logs be shipped to our S3 or Splunk/Kafka?
03:35 Jamal Ortiz: logs can be routed to your logging sink — S3, CloudWatch, or external SIEM. retention is configurable. we can also stream audit events to your Kinesis/Firehose.
03:45 Maya Lin: fantastic. what about latency? we run low-latency inference for interactive features, 100-200ms target for short prompts. any numbers you can share?
03:55 Jamal Ortiz: latency depends on model and instance type. for a mid-size open model on A100-like instances we typically see 80-150ms p95 for short prompts when served in-region. batching and KV cache can reduce cost but add a ms tail. if you need sub-50ms we can discuss specialized hardware and colocated endpoints.
04:18 Carlos Ruiz: KV cache? do you mean KV cache — we've seen reference to KV cash in some notes. how is cache shared?
04:23 Jamal Ortiz: sorry, kv cache — it's per-request session caching stored in the serving instance's memory or a dedicated cache layer depending on topology. for privacy we keep KV in the customer VPC; nothing goes to our shared cache unless you opt-in for cross-request caching.
04:37 Maya Lin: any limitations on CIDR ranges or overlapping networks for peering? we have overlapping address spaces with some partners.
04:45 Jamal Ortiz: overlapping CIDRs complicate peering. options: TGW with route table translation, NAT/Proxy, or AWS PrivateLink which avoids route propagation. we'll capture your CIDRs and recommend the cleanest approach in the workshop.
04:58 Erin Patel: do you have a preferred timeline for a pilot?
05:02 Maya Lin: we'd like a small pilot in January: 2-3 models, a handful of endpoints in eu-west-1, and a 2-week benchmark. budget approval is likely in place, so timeline is tight.
05:12 Jamal Ortiz: that should be doable. we'll propose a pilot plan and required infra changes. typically pilot takes 2-3 weeks to provision and test networking.
05:20 Priya Desai: data residency proof — we'll need an attestation that inference traces and logs remain in eu-west-1 and that keys never leave our KMS.
05:28 Jamal Ortiz: we can provide a design doc and attestation as part of the security pack. some customers ask for an on-prem audit; we have templates for SOC2 artifacts.
05:36 Maya Lin: what about cross-account role assumptions? we prefer granting minimal IAM and not wholesale account-level trusts.
05:43 Jamal Ortiz: we recommend cross-account IAM roles with least privilege for provisioning and a short-lived assume-role pattern. we can do a deploy-user or CloudFormation stack in your account so you keep full control.
05:55 Carlos Ruiz: do you support private DNS resolution for internal service names?
06:00 Jamal Ortiz: yes, using PrivateLink or endpoint services plus endpoint-specific DNS entries you can resolve internal hosts. we'll include Terraform/CFN snippets.
06:10 Erin Patel: any regulatory flags? HIPAA/PCI?
06:14 Priya Desai: we handle healthcare PII in some workloads and will need BAAs and relevant controls mapped.
06:19 Jamal Ortiz: we have a healthcare package and BAAs available for enterprise customers on Private. will include that in the security docs.
06:26 Maya Lin: cost implications — what's the difference between running on Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?
06:31 Erin Patel: Hosted is pay-as-you-go and fastest to get started, but for strict VPC and KMS requirements you need Private. Dedicated gives reserved capacity without full private networking. Private has higher one-time setup and a platform fee but gives control and predictable costs. Jamal can share a sizing+cost worksheet.
06:48 Jamal Ortiz: exactly — for pilot we'll recommend instance types and expected token costs; we'll also show batching trade-offs.
06:55 Maya Lin: excellent. small thing — do you support provider-specific features like AWS Nitro Enclaves or custom AMI images?
07:02 Jamal Ortiz: Nitro Enclaves is not a mainstream config yet for our runtime, but we can explore a specialized build. custom AMIs are possible for on-prem or dedicated hosts.
07:12 Priya Desai: encryption-in-transit details? TLS mutual auth?
07:16 Jamal Ortiz: mTLS is supported for internal endpoints. we can also terminate TLS at the NLB and use internal mTLS for node-to-node. key rotation schedule is configurable.
07:26 Erin Patel: getting close to time. to recap: you want a Private deployment in eu-west-1, VPC endpoint or TGW solution to avoid public egress, customer-managed KMS, logs shipped to your SIEM, and a pilot in Jan for 2 weeks. next steps are security pack, network checklist, and an SE design workshop in early Jan.
07:46 Maya Lin: yep that sums it up.
07:49 Carlos Ruiz: thanks, we'll pull CIDRs and share behind the ticket.
07:53 Priya Desai: and we'll send compliance Qs.
07:56 Erin Patel: perfect. I'll follow up with the security pack and a proposed workshop times. thanks all, happy new year early.
07:63 Jamal Ortiz: thanks everyone.
---
Notes: transcript contains several minor transcription errors (typical of automated captions) — e.g., "KV cash" for KV cache, product names occasionally mis-attributed. Links referenced during call: security pack (link to sent email), pilot sizing worksheet (link), template network diagram (attached in follow-up).
additional_notes: Customer emphasized EU residency and zero-public-egress. AE/SE pair recommended Private with TGW or PrivateLink depending on CIDR overlaps. Agreed to SE workshop and pilot. Security pack/share will include SOC2, BAA and KMS integration pattern.
